pages.tutorial.title: Reflection of Light
pages.tutorial.complete_title: You know how this works now.
pages.tutorial.stage.observe.name: Observe
pages.tutorial.stage.observe.instruction: Grab the mirror and rotate it. Watch the orange beam bounce — the two angles around the dotted normal always stay equal.
pages.tutorial.stage.observe.concept: Law of reflection: $\theta_i = \theta_r$ — the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
pages.tutorial.stage.experiment.name: Experiment
pages.tutorial.stage.experiment.instruct: Aim the mirror, then press Fire (or Space) to shoot the beam. Each star shows ∠, its angle from the source measured at the mirror. Light all 3 stars — you have 7 shots.
pages.tutorial.stage.experiment.concept: You aim only by controlling the mirror's angle.
pages.tutorial.stage.evaluate.name: Evaluate
pages.tutorial.stage.evaluate.instructio: The beam is invisible. Read the coordinates of $S$, $M$ and $T$, compute the mirror angle $\varphi$ that sends the beam onto the target, set the mirror, then Fire. Peek reveals your current $\varphi$ so you can verify your calculation.
pages.tutorial.stage.evaluate.concept: The mirror is perpendicular to the bisector of the angle formed by $\overrightarrow{MS}$ and $\overrightarrow{MT}$.
pages.tutorial.scene.exhausted: OUT OF SHOTS · RESET TO RETRY
pages.tutorial.scene.tip2: aim, then press SPACE to fire
pages.tutorial.scene.tip3: compute φ from coordinates, then fire
pages.tutorial.tour.welcome.title: This is a real exercise
pages.tutorial.tour.welcome.body: Not a demo — this is exactly what every one of the 125 exercises looks like. Two minutes and you'll know how all of them work.
pages.tutorial.tour.canvas.title: The canvas
pages.tutorial.tour.canvas.body: Every exercise is a small simulation. You learn by moving things and watching what happens — not by reading.
pages.tutorial.tour.rail.title: Three stages, always
pages.tutorial.tour.rail.body: **Observe** → **Experiment** → **Evaluate**. Every exercise follows this arc, and the last one is different from the first two in a way that matters. More on that when we get there.
pages.tutorial.tour.instruction.title: Your task
pages.tutorial.tour.instruction.body: Always here, at the top of the rail. Read it before touching anything — it tells you exactly what this stage wants.
pages.tutorial.tour.concept.title: The physics you need
pages.tutorial.tour.concept.body: The law in play, stated plainly. Here it is the law of reflection: $\theta_i = \theta_r$ — light bounces off at the same angle it arrives.
pages.tutorial.tour.hud-tl.title: Corner readouts
pages.tutorial.tour.hud-tl.body: The four corners of the canvas carry live information. Top-left is always which stage you are on.
pages.tutorial.tour.hud-tr.title: Live measurements
pages.tutorial.tour.hud-tr.body: Top-right shows what the simulation is measuring right now — here, the two angles. Watch this number as you move things.
pages.tutorial.tour.fullscreen.title: More room
pages.tutorial.tour.fullscreen.body: This corner button blows the canvas up to fill your screen — worth it on a phone, where the scene is small and you need to aim precisely.
pages.tutorial.tour.controls.title: Your controls
pages.tutorial.tour.controls.body: **Retry** resets the stage if you get tangled. **Next** unlocks once you have done what the stage asks.
pages.tutorial.tour.source.title: The light source
pages.tutorial.tour.source.body: Call it $S$. A beam leaves here and travels to the mirror.
pages.tutorial.tour.mirror-intro.title: The mirror
pages.tutorial.tour.mirror-intro.body: Call it $M$. The two teal dots are its ends — grab either one to rotate it.
pages.tutorial.tour.mirror-drag.title: Rotate it
pages.tutorial.tour.mirror-drag.body: Drag the mirror around and watch the orange beam swing. Notice the reflected beam moves **twice** as fast as the mirror does.
pages.tutorial.tour.normal.title: The normal
pages.tutorial.tour.normal.body: The dotted line is the **normal** — an imaginary line perpendicular to the mirror surface. Every angle in reflection is measured from it, never from the mirror itself.
pages.tutorial.tour.arcs.title: The law, on screen
pages.tutorial.tour.arcs.body: The two teal arcs are the angle in ($\theta_i$) and the angle out ($\theta_r$), both measured from the normal. Keep dragging — they stay equal no matter what you do. **That is the whole law.**
pages.tutorial.tour.stage1-done.title: That was Observe
pages.tutorial.tour.stage1-done.body: You did not calculate anything — you watched a rule hold. That is what stage 1 is for. Hit **Next**.
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-intro.title: Stage 2 — Experiment
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-intro.body: Now you use the law instead of watching it. The help is still on screen, but you have a job to do.
pages.tutorial.tour.stars.title: Three targets
pages.tutorial.tour.stars.body: Light all three stars by bouncing the beam onto them.
pages.tutorial.tour.fire-intro.title: The beam is not continuous now
pages.tutorial.tour.fire-intro.body: You aim first, then shoot. Press **FIRE** — or the spacebar — to send one pulse along your current aim.
pages.tutorial.tour.shots.title: Shots are limited
pages.tutorial.tour.shots.body: Seven shots for three stars. Aiming carelessly costs you one, so line the beam up before firing — that is the point of the constraint.
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-play.title: Light all three
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-play.body: Each star is labelled ∠ — the angle at the mirror between the source and that star. Top right, $\theta_i$ shows the angle of incidence you are currently set to. **One tells you the other.** Work it out, aim until the readout matches, then fire.
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-done.title: That was Experiment
pages.tutorial.tour.stage2-done.body: You applied the law to hit something on purpose — still with the beam visible to guide you. Hit **Next**, and read the following screen carefully.
pages.tutorial.tour.stage3-warning.title: Stage 3 is different. Read this.
pages.tutorial.tour.stage3-warning.body: The help you have been leaning on is **gone — deliberately.** No visible beam before you fire, no angle arcs, no live feedback. This is not the app breaking. It is the exercise asking whether you actually understood, instead of whether you can nudge things until they work.
pages.tutorial.tour.get-paper.title: Get a pencil and paper
pages.tutorial.tour.get-paper.body: Seriously — right now. Every Evaluate stage in this app is designed to be worked out on paper first, then checked in the simulation. If you can finish one without writing anything down, the exercise was built wrong.
pages.tutorial.tour.coords.title: Everything you need is on screen
pages.tutorial.tour.coords.body: A grid appeared, and the three points are labelled: the source $S\,(100,\ 350)$, the mirror $M\,(400,\ 200)$, and the target $T\,(700,\ 350)$. Write them down.
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-1.title: Set up the calculation
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-1.body: The concept panel gives you the rule: the mirror must be **perpendicular to the bisector** of the angle formed by $\overrightarrow{MS}$ and $\overrightarrow{MT}$. So find those two directions first.
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-2.title: Two directions
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-2.body: From $M\,(400,200)$: $\overrightarrow{MS} = (-300,\ 150)$, which points at $153.4°$. And $\overrightarrow{MT} = (300,\ 150)$, which points at $26.6°$.
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-3.title: Bisect, then turn 90°
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-3.body: The bisector is the average: $(153.4° + 26.6°)/2 = 90°$ — straight up. The mirror is perpendicular to it, so $\varphi = 90° - 90° = \mathbf{0°}$. **Level.**
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-check.title: Sanity-check it
pages.tutorial.tour.calc-check.body: Look at the numbers again: $S$ and $T$ are both at height $350$, with $M$ below them at $200$. The picture is symmetric — so of course a level mirror sends the beam from one to the other. Always check whether your answer makes sense before you trust it.
pages.tutorial.tour.set-mirror.title: Now set the mirror to 0°
pages.tutorial.tour.set-mirror.body: Drag it level. You cannot see the beam, so use **Peek** in the controls — it reveals your current $\varphi$ so you can check your setting against your calculation. Peek never gives you the answer.
pages.tutorial.tour.fire-final.title: Fire
pages.tutorial.tour.fire-final.body: Your calculation says this hits. Find out.
pages.tutorial.tour.second-target.title: The second one is yours
pages.tutorial.tour.second-target.body: A new target appeared, and this time nobody walks you through it. Same method: read the coordinates, find the two directions, bisect, subtract $90°$. Paper first.
pages.tutorial.tour.second-target.waitin: Hit the second target to finish
pages.tutorial.tour.finish.title: That's the whole model
pages.tutorial.tour.finish.body: **Observe** shows you the rule. **Experiment** makes you use it with help still on. **Evaluate** takes the help away and asks if you understood. All 125 exercises work exactly like this — different physics, same shape.
